newsitem.title: FRANCE: Suez shares sink on expectation of bid.
newsitem.headline: Suez shares sink on expectation of bid.

text.p: Shares in French holding company Cie de Suez fell on Monday afternoon on expectations that the company would launch a bid to acquire water utility Lyonnaise des Eaux, whose shares were up significantly, traders said.

"The market is betting on the fact that the merger will take place and that Suez will absorb Lyonnaise des Eaux, which means Suez will have to pay a premium to encourage that merger," a trader said. "I couldn't understand why Suez was up this morning."
Suez shares were down 1.39 percent at 276.50 francs while Lyonnaise shares were up 2.32 percent at 574 francs at 1530 GMT.
The two firms' shares had risen sharply in early trading on reports a merger deal would be drafted in time for a presentation to the Suez board meeting on April 1.

Analysts said any merger likely would be structured to enable Suez to bid for Lyonnaise, as it is the larger firm and has cash and important unused tax losses which would be lost if Suez were acquired by Lyonnaise.
